title: Coverage diagnostics: bootstrap SE versus empirical SE
code: run_one <- function(seed) {   sim <- generate_aft_data(n = N_MAIN, n_val = N_VAL, seed = seed)   boot <- two_stage_bootstrap(     survival   = sim$survival,     validation = sim$validation,     x_var      = "X_true",     covariates = names(V_REF), v_ref = V_REF,     df         = DF,     lambda     = c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2),     B = B_INNER, R = R_BOOT,     x_grid = x_grid   )   list(     f_hat   = boot$f_hat,     width   = boot$upper - boot$lower,     covered = as.integer(truth >= boot$lower & truth <= boot$upper)   ) }

title: Coverage diagnostics: bootstrap SE versus empirical SE
code: t0 <- Sys.time() res <- lapply(seq_len(N_REP), function(i) run_one(20260601L + i)) elapsed <- Sys.time() - t0 elapsed #> Time difference of 3.2952 mins

title: Coverage diagnostics: bootstrap SE versus empirical SE
text: grid point, bootstrap CI width implies normal-approximation SE width / (2 * 1.96). empirical SE Monte Carlo SD single-fit f_hat across replicates. full coverage study (N_REP = 100, R_BOOT = 200) ratio 0.999 (full grid) 1.000 (interior) — bootstrap honest.
code: width_mat <- do.call(cbind, lapply(res, `[[`, "width")) fhat_mat  <- do.call(cbind, lapply(res, `[[`, "f_hat"))  se_boot <- rowMeans(width_mat) / (2 * qnorm(0.975)) se_emp  <- apply(fhat_mat, 1, sd)  interior <- x_grid >= quantile(x_grid, 0.05) &             x_grid <= quantile(x_grid, 0.95)  data.frame(   region  = c("Full grid", "Interior 5-95"),   SE_boot = round(c(mean(se_boot),           mean(se_boot[interior])), 3),   SE_emp  = round(c(mean(se_emp),            mean(se_emp[interior])), 3),   ratio   = round(c(mean(se_boot) / mean(se_emp),                     mean(se_boot[interior]) / mean(se_emp[interior])), 3) ) #>          region SE_boot SE_emp ratio #> 1     Full grid   0.098  0.090 1.079 #> 2 Interior 5-95   0.101  0.095 1.065

title: Simulation study: Oracle vs Naive vs SIMEX
code: run_one <- function(seed) {   sim <- generate_aft_data(n = N, n_val = N_VAL, seed = seed)   cal <- fit_me_calibration(sim$validation)   W   <- as.matrix(sim$survival[, cal$W_cols])   g   <- gls_combine(W, cal)   dat <- sim$survival   dat$W_bar <- g$W_bar    fit_oracle <- fit_aft_spline(dat, "X_true",                                covariates = names(V_REF), df = DF)   fit_naive  <- fit_aft_spline(dat, "W_bar",                                covariates = names(V_REF), df = DF)   lp_oracle <- predict_curve(fit_oracle, x_grid, V_REF, "X_true")   lp_naive  <- predict_curve(fit_naive,  x_grid, V_REF, "W_bar")    s <- simex_aft_spline(dat, x_var = "W_bar",                         sigma_w_sq = g$sigma_w_sq,                         covariates = names(V_REF), v_ref = V_REF,                         lambda = LAMBDA, B = B_INNER,                         x_grid = x_grid)   list(Oracle = lp_oracle - lp_oracle[1],        Naive  = lp_naive  - lp_naive[1],        SIMEX  = s$curve_simex) }

title: Simulation study: Oracle vs Naive vs SIMEX
text: pattern matches manuscript: Naive carries 2-3x ISE Oracle (attenuation), SIMEX recovers gap.
code: methods <- c("Oracle", "Naive", "SIMEX") ise_mat <- sapply(res, function(r)   vapply(methods, function(m) {     e <- r[[m]] - truth     delta_x <- diff(x_grid)     sum(((e[-1] + e[-length(e)])^2 / 4) * delta_x)   }, numeric(1)) ) rownames(ise_mat) <- methods data.frame(   Mean   = round(rowMeans(ise_mat), 3),   MCSE   = round(apply(ise_mat, 1, sd) / sqrt(N_REP), 4),   Median = round(apply(ise_mat, 1, median), 3) ) #>         Mean   MCSE Median #> Oracle 0.065 0.0108  0.043 #> Naive  0.181 0.0254  0.140 #> SIMEX  0.084 0.0162  0.057

title: Simulation study: Oracle vs Naive vs SIMEX
code: mean_curve <- function(m) rowMeans(sapply(res, function(r) r[[m]])) fits <- setNames(lapply(methods, mean_curve), methods) plot_curves(x_grid, truth, fits,             title = "Mean SIMEX / Naive / Oracle curves across simulated replicates")

title: AFT + Spline + SIMEX for Nonlinear Dose-Response with Multivariate Measurement Error
text: aftsplex implements two-phase estimator: Phase 1. Multivariate linear measurement-error calibration external validation sample paired (truth, surrogate) observations: log W*_ij = alpha_0j + alpha_1j * log W_i + e_ij. GLS combiner weights back-transformed surrogates single calibrated exposure conditional variance. Phase 2. Natural-cubic-spline AFT model calibrated exposure, corrected residual attenuation via SIMEX (Cook Stefanski, 1994). Inference uses nested two-stage nonparametric bootstrap resamples validation main-study samples jointly, addressing plug--variance critique applies whenever validation sample small relative main study.

title: AFT + Spline + SIMEX for Nonlinear Dose-Response with Multivariate Measurement Error
text: Carroll, R. J., Kuchenhoff, H., Lombard, F., & Stefanski, L. . (1996). Asymptotics SIMEX estimator nonlinear measurement-error models. Journal American Statistical Association, 91, 242-250. Cook, J. R., & Stefanski, L. . (1994). Simulation-extrapolation estimation parametric measurement-error models. Journal American Statistical Association, 89, 1314-1328.

text: Implements simulation-extrapolation (Cook Stefanski 1994; Carroll, Kuchenhoff, Lombard Stefanski 1996) natural-cubic-spline AFT model fitted fit_aft_spline(). lambda supplied grid, draws B perturbed surrogates additional noise sqrt(lambda * sigma_w_sq) * N(0, 1), refits, averages centred linear predictor across B, extrapolates lambda = -1 via pointwise quadratic OLS.

title: SIMEX-correct the AFT-spline dose-response curve — simex_aft_spline
code: simex_aft_spline(   data,   x_var,   sigma_w_sq,   covariates = character(0),   v_ref = NULL,   df = 4,   knots = NULL,   outcome_var = "T_obs",   status_var = "delta",   lambda = c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2),   B = 50,   dist = "lognormal",   x_grid = NULL,   verbose = FALSE,   maxiter = 200 )

title: SIMEX-correct the AFT-spline dose-response curve — simex_aft_spline
code: # \donttest{ sim <- generate_aft_data(n = 500, n_val = 200, seed = 1) cal <- fit_me_calibration(sim$validation) W   <- as.matrix(sim$survival[, cal$W_cols]) g   <- gls_combine(W, cal) dat <- sim$survival dat$W_bar <- g$W_bar s <- simex_aft_spline(dat, x_var = "W_bar",                       sigma_w_sq = g$sigma_w_sq,                       covariates = c("V1","V2","V3","V4"),                       v_ref = c(V1=30, V2=30, V3=0, V4=0),                       lambda = c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2), B = 10) head(s$curve_simex) #>          1          2          3          4          5          6  #> 0.00000000 0.02254499 0.04499498 0.06737831 0.08972246 0.11205485  # }

what: Two-stage nonparametric bootstrap for the SIMEX-corrected curve — two_stage_bootstrap
title: Two-stage nonparametric bootstrap for the SIMEX-corrected curve — two_stage_bootstrap
text: replicate r: resample validation participants; refit multivariate calibration via fit_me_calibration(); resample main-study participants; form bootstrap-combined surrogate via gls_combine() refit calibration; run simex_aft_spline() refit sigma_w_sq store corrected curve.

NULL covariates. surrogate_pattern Regex used identify surrogate columns; default "^W[0-9]+$". df, knots, lambda, B, dist Passed simex_aft_spline(). outcome_var, status_var Passed simex_aft_spline(). R Number outer bootstrap replicates. x_grid Numeric exposure grid curve. NULL, taken 100 equally spaced points 2nd 98th percentile full-sample combined surrogate. verbose Print progress bar?

title: Two-stage nonparametric bootstrap for the SIMEX-corrected curve — two_stage_bootstrap
text: list elements x_grid exposure grid, f_hat single-fit SIMEX point estimate (full-sample, resampling), bs_mean mean bootstrap curves, curves matrix bootstrap curves (length(x_grid) rows R cols), median, lower, upper percentile-CI summaries (2.5%, 50%, 97.5%), lower_basic, upper_basic reverse-percentile (basic) CI bounds, f_bc bias-corrected point estimate 2*f_hat - bs_mean, sigma_w_sq_boot, omega_boot per-replicate Phase-1 summaries, R_effective number replicates produced curve. Empirically (see vignette("coverage-diagnostics")) percentile CI primary interval; basic CI kept completeness improve coverage simulated diminishing-returns curves dominant residual bias spline smoothing rather SIMEX.

title: Two-stage nonparametric bootstrap for the SIMEX-corrected curve — two_stage_bootstrap
text: Pointwise quantiles across r give CIs propagate Phase-1 Phase-2 uncertainty - addresses plug--variance critique conditional sigma_w_sq alone yields anti-conservative intervals validation sample small relative main study.

code: # \donttest{ sim <- generate_aft_data(n = 500, n_val = 200, seed = 1) boot <- two_stage_bootstrap(   survival   = sim$survival,   validation = sim$validation,   x_var      = "X_true",   covariates = c("V1","V2","V3","V4"),   v_ref      = c(V1=30, V2=30, V3=0, V4=0),   lambda     = c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2), B = 5, R = 10 ) head(boot$f_hat) #>          1          2          3          4          5          6  #> 0.00000000 0.01912404 0.03855214 0.05830025 0.07838434 0.09882034  # }
